# Mengyuan (Marvin) Li

Assistant Professor, University of Southern California

[Thomas Lord Department of Computer Science](https://www.cs.usc.edu/)
[Ming Hsieh Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering](https://minghsiehece.usc.edu/)

Recruiting **PhD students for Fall 2027.** USC MS and undergraduate students are also welcome. [Join SEPT Lab](https://mengyuanli.com/#join)

I lead [SEPT Lab](https://septlab.com/) (Security, Privacy, and Trust) at USC. My research builds trustworthy computing environments by integrating hardware security mechanisms with software systems, so that data and computation stay protected on platforms from personal devices to cloud AI systems.

- **Research areas:** Verifiable AI systems · Trusted execution environments (TEEs) · Confidential computing · System and hardware security · AI agent security
- **Lab:** [SEPT Lab](https://septlab.com/) · [verifiable.pro](https://verifiable.pro/) · [SEPT Lab on GitHub](https://github.com/sept-usc)
- **Profiles:** [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=cgjqyuoAAAAJ&hl=en) · [DBLP](https://dblp.org/pid/157/4437-4.html) · [USC Viterbi profile](https://viterbi.usc.edu/directory/faculty/Li/Mengyuan)
- **Email:** [mengyuanli@usc.edu](mailto:mengyuanli@usc.edu)

## About

Mengyuan (Marvin) Li is an Assistant Professor in the Thomas Lord Department of Computer Science at the University of Southern California, where he leads [SEPT Lab](https://septlab.com/) (Security, Privacy, and Trust). Before joining USC in 2024, he was a postdoctoral researcher at [MIT CSAIL](https://www.csail.mit.edu/) (2022–2024), working with Prof. [Mengjia Yan](https://people.csail.mit.edu/mengjia/). He received his Ph.D. in Computer Science and Engineering from [The Ohio State University](https://www.osu.edu/) in 2022, advised by Prof. [Yinqian Zhang](https://yinqian.org/). His research on AMD SEV led to several AMD security bulletins and CVEs, and his paper CROSSLINE received the Best Paper Award Runner-Up at ACM CCS 2021.

## Research

My group pursues two research thrusts:

- Uncovering, understanding, and defending against system and hardware vulnerabilities in cloud systems, CPUs, GPUs, and AI systems.
- Co-designing software and hardware for secure and efficient AI systems.

**Research directions:**

- **[Verifiable AI](https://mengyuanli.com/verifiable-ai.html)**
  Evidence that an AI result came from the claimed model and computation, produced without revealing sensitive data. SEPT Lab also maintains [verifiable.pro](https://verifiable.pro/), a public resource with news, explainers, and guides on verifiable AI.
  *Topics:* zero-knowledge verification · LLM inference · model oversight
- **[TEE and Confidential Computing](https://mengyuanli.com/tee-confidential-computing.html)**
  Practical hardware-isolated execution: efficient and secure TEE-based systems for cloud and AI workloads, from oblivious memory inside VM-based TEEs to confidential multi-GPU machine learning.
  *Topics:* AMD SEV-SNP · Intel SGX · confidential VMs and GPUs · ORAM
- **[System and Hardware Vulnerabilities](https://mengyuanli.com/tee-confidential-computing.html#attacks)**
  Design flaws and side channels that break the security guarantees of systems and hardware, found and disclosed to vendors such as AMD.
  *Topics:* side channels · SEV-SNP · macOS sandboxing · GPUs
- **[AI Agent Security](https://mengyuanli.com/ai-agent-security.html)**
  Observing and protecting agent execution with TEEs and runtime monitoring, so that agents can be trusted with sensitive data on shared infrastructure.
  *Topics:* runtime monitoring · tool isolation · agent memory

**Related:** [SEPT Lab research overview](https://septlab.com/research.html) · [verifiable.pro](https://verifiable.pro/)

## Join SEPT Lab

Recruiting for Fall 2027

**PhD students:** For Fall 2027, [Yue Zhao](https://viterbi-web.usc.edu/~yzhao010/), [Ruolin Li](https://ruolinli.me/), and I are recruiting up to six PhD students together through a research cluster that spans our departments. Ruolin Li works on autonomous systems and Yue Zhao on trustworthy AI, while my group focuses on systems and security. Our shared goal is intelligent systems that remain reliable and secure when they are deployed in the real world. Students in the cluster can work with more than one of us and pursue questions that cross our research areas. Co-advising is possible but not required.

To apply, submit your application through USC Viterbi Graduate Admission ([PhD application information](https://viterbigradadmission.usc.edu/doctoral/)). If you are interested in working with me, email [mengyuanli@usc.edu](mailto:mengyuanli@usc.edu?subject=%5BSEPT%20PhD%5D) with “[SEPT PhD]” in the subject line.

**Research collaboration:** Current USC MS and undergraduate students are welcome to work on research projects in SEPT Lab, and students at other universities can apply to collaborate with us. If you are interested, email [mengyuanli@usc.edu](mailto:mengyuanli@usc.edu?subject=%5BSEPT%20Research%5D) with “[SEPT Research]” in the subject line.

# TEE and Confidential Computing

Mengyuan Li’s research on trusted execution environments (TEEs) and confidential computing spans four related areas: [TEE-based systems and their performance](https://mengyuanli.com/tee-confidential-computing.html#systems), [attacks on confidential computing platforms](https://mengyuanli.com/tee-confidential-computing.html#attacks), [defenses for secure cloud and AI infrastructure](https://mengyuanli.com/tee-confidential-computing.html#defenses), and [general cloud security](https://mengyuanli.com/tee-confidential-computing.html#cloud).

Topics: AMD SEV and SEV-SNP · Intel SGX · confidential VMs · cloud GPU security · ciphertext side channels · virtualization · secure networking · serverless platforms

## Systems

- **[MC-ORAM: A Mask-Assisted and Counter-Based Non-Deterministic ORAM Inside VM-Based TEEs](https://doi.org/10.1109/ISCA66397.2026.00047)**
  Yongqin Wang, Rachit Rajat, Jonghyun Lee, **Mengyuan Li**, Murali Annavaram
  *53rd ACM/IEEE Annual International Symposium on Computer Architecture (ISCA 2026)*
  Explores secure memory techniques for VM-based TEEs and efficient protected execution.
  [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1109/ISCA66397.2026.00047) · [BibTeX](https://mengyuanli.com/files/bib/mc-oram-isca26.bib)
- **[SCALE: Tackling Communication Bottlenecks in Confidential Distributed Machine Learning](https://doi.org/10.1109/HPCA68181.2026.11408582)**
  Joongun Park, Yongqin Wang, Huan Xu, Hanjiang Wu, **Mengyuan Li**, Tushar Krishna
  *2026 IEEE International Symposium on High-Performance Computer Architecture (HPCA 2026)*
  Connects confidential computing with efficient multi-GPU machine learning and shows how to reduce system bottlenecks in trusted infrastructure.
  [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1109/HPCA68181.2026.11408582) · [BibTeX](https://mengyuanli.com/files/bib/scale-hpca26.bib)
- **[Query Cost Model Calibration in Confidential Virtual Machines](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26385)**
  Qihan Zhang, **Mengyuan Li**, Ibrahim Sabek
  *Workshop on Secure and Private Data Management (SeQureDB 2026)*
  Narrows the slowdown of analytical queries in confidential VMs such as AMD SEV-SNP with a lightweight calibration of the query optimizer’s cost model for data movement and RMP-related translation.
  [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.26385) · [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26385) · [BibTeX](https://mengyuanli.com/files/bib/cvm-query-cost-sequredb26.bib)
- **[OTRO: Oblivious Tokenization Path with Square-Root ORAM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17358)**
  Jonghyun Lee, Yongqin Wang, Rachit Rajat, Daniel Wong, **Mengyuan Li**, Murali Annavaram
  *arXiv preprint arXiv:2606.17358*
  Reduces access-pattern leakage from the CPU-side tokenizer in confidential LLM serving with replicated square-root ORAM, adding at most 4.5% to time-to-first-token in an Intel TDX confidential VM with an NVIDIA H100 GPU.
  [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.17358) · [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17358) · [BibTeX](https://mengyuanli.com/files/bib/otro-arxiv26.bib)
- **[Infrastructure for Valuable, Tradable, and Verifiable Agent Memory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.24564)**
  **Mengyuan Li**, Lei Gao, Haoxuan Xu, Jiate Li, Potung Yu, Lingke Cheng, Yue Zhao, Murali Annavaram
  *arXiv preprint arXiv:2603.24564*
  Proposes infrastructure that makes agent memory verifiable and tradable: ClawGang binds memory to verifiable computational provenance through TEE remote attestation, and MeowTrade is a market layer for listing, transferring, and governing certified memory artifacts.
  [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.24564) · [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.24564) · [Code](https://github.com/sept-usc/ClawGang) · [BibTeX](https://mengyuanli.com/files/bib/agent-memory-arxiv26.bib)
- **[Ditto: Elastic Confidential VMs with Secure and Dynamic CPU Scaling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.15542)**
  Shixuan Zhao\*, **Mengyuan Li**\*, Mengjia Yan, Zhiqiang Lin
  *arXiv preprint arXiv:2409.15542*
  Explores how to support elastic confidential VMs with secure and dynamic CPU scaling, improving the flexibility and efficiency of TEE-based systems.
  [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2409.15542) · [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.15542) · [BibTeX](https://mengyuanli.com/files/bib/ditto-arxiv24.bib)
- **[Bridge the Future: High-Performance Networks in Confidential VMs without Trusted I/O devices](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.03360)**
  **Mengyuan Li**, Shashvat Srivastava, Mengjia Yan
  *arXiv preprint arXiv:2403.03360*
  Studies how to improve networking performance for confidential VMs without relying on trusted I/O devices, targeting practical system optimization in confidential cloud settings.
  [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2403.03360) · [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.03360) · [BibTeX](https://mengyuanli.com/files/bib/bridge-the-future-arxiv24.bib)
- **[vSGX: Virtualizing SGX Enclaves on AMD SEV](https://doi.org/10.1109/SP46214.2022.9833694)**
  Shixuan Zhao, **Mengyuan Li**, Yinqian Zhang, Zhiqiang Lin
  *2022 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (S&P 2022)*
  Bridges virtualization and enclave protection across TEE platforms, highlighting system support for deployable trusted execution.
  [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1109/SP46214.2022.9833694) · [PDF](https://yinqian.org/papers/sp22a.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/OSUSecLab/vSGX) · [BibTeX](https://mengyuanli.com/files/bib/vsgx-sp22.bib)

\* Equal contribution.

## Attacks

- **[A Close Look at RMP Entry Caching and Its Security Implications in SEV-SNP](https://doi.org/10.1145/3768725.3768727)**
  Alexis Bagia, Vincent Quentin Ulitzsch, Daniël Trujillo, **Mengyuan Li**, Mengjia Yan, Jean-Pierre Seifert
  *14th International Workshop on Hardware and Architectural Support for Security and Privacy (HASP 2025)*
  Examines the security implications of RMP entry caching in SEV-SNP and expands the attack surface analysis of confidential computing platforms.
  Disclosures: [AMD-SB-3036](https://www.amd.com/en/resources/product-security/bulletin/amd-sb-3036.html)
  [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1145/3768725.3768727) · [BibTeX](https://mengyuanli.com/files/bib/rmp-caching-hasp25.bib)
- **[PWRLEAK: Exploiting Power Reporting Interface for Side-Channel Attacks on AMD SEV](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-35504-2_3)**
  Wubing Wang, **Mengyuan Li**, Yinqian Zhang, Zhiqiang Lin
  *20th Conference on Detection of Intrusions and Malware & Vulnerability Assessment (DIMVA 2023)*
  Demonstrates a side-channel attack surface exposed by the power reporting interface in AMD SEV platforms.
  Disclosures: [AMD-SB-3004](https://www.amd.com/en/resources/product-security/bulletin/amd-sb-3004.html) · [CVE-2023-20575](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2023-20575)
  [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-35504-2_3) · [PDF](https://yinqian.org/papers/dimva23.pdf) · [BibTeX](https://mengyuanli.com/files/bib/pwrleak-dimva23.bib)
- **[A Systematic Look at Ciphertext Side Channels on AMD SEV-SNP](https://doi.org/10.1109/SP46214.2022.9833768)**
  **Mengyuan Li**\*, Luca Wilke\*, Jan Wichelmann, Thomas Eisenbarth, Radu Teodorescu, Yinqian Zhang
  *2022 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (S&P 2022)*
  Studies side-channel vulnerabilities that break confidentiality guarantees in encrypted and confidential execution settings.
  Disclosures: [AMD-SB-1033](https://www.amd.com/en/resources/product-security/bulletin/amd-sb-1033.html) · [CVE-2021-46744](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2021-46744)
  AMD published an official white paper for TEE developers and users on writing code that resists ciphertext side channels. [AMD white paper](https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/resources/bulletin/technical-guidance-for-mitigating-effects-of-ciphertext-visibility-under-amd-sev.pdf)
  [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1109/SP46214.2022.9833768) · [PDF](https://yinqian.org/papers/sp22b.pdf) · [BibTeX](https://mengyuanli.com/files/bib/ciphertext-sev-snp-sp22.bib)
- **[TLB Poisoning Attacks on AMD Secure Encrypted Virtualization](https://doi.org/10.1145/3485832.3485876)**
  **Mengyuan Li**, Yinqian Zhang, Huibo Wang, Kang Li, Yueqiang Cheng
  *37th Annual Computer Security Applications Conference (ACSAC 2021)*
  Uncovers a microarchitectural attack that breaks isolation assumptions in AMD SEV through TLB manipulation.
  Disclosures: [AMD-SB-1023](https://www.amd.com/en/resources/product-security/bulletin/amd-sb-1023.html) · [CVE-2021-26340](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2021-26340) · [Lenovo LEN-75179](https://support.lenovo.com/us/en/product_security/LEN-75179)
  [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1145/3485832.3485876) · [PDF](https://yinqian.org/papers/acsac21.pdf) · [BibTeX](https://mengyuanli.com/files/bib/tlb-poisoning-acsac21.bib)
- **[CROSSLINE: Breaking “Security-by-Crash” based Memory Isolation in AMD SEV](https://doi.org/10.1145/3460120.3485253)**
  **Mengyuan Li**, Yinqian Zhang, Zhiqiang Lin
  *2021 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS 2021)*
  Shows how crash-based isolation assumptions can fail in AMD SEV and lead to cross-boundary memory exposure.
  **Best Paper Award Runner-Up**
  [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1145/3460120.3485253) · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2008.00146) · [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.00146) · [BibTeX](https://mengyuanli.com/files/bib/crossline-ccs21.bib)
- **[CIPHERLEAKS: Breaking Constant-time Cryptography on AMD SEV via the Ciphertext Side Channel](https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity21/presentation/li-mengyuan)**
  **Mengyuan Li**, Yinqian Zhang, Huibo Wang, Kang Li, Yueqiang Cheng
  *30th USENIX Security Symposium (USENIX Security 2021)*
  Shows how ciphertext side channels can break constant-time cryptographic implementations running inside AMD SEV.
  Disclosures: [AMD-SB-1013](https://www.amd.com/en/resources/product-security/bulletin/amd-sb-1013.html) · [CVE-2020-12966](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2020-12966)
  AMD filed an embargo for the ciphertext side channel identified in the paper and announced a security bulletin together with a hardware patch for SEV-SNP in August 2021.
  [Paper](https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity21/presentation/li-mengyuan) · [PDF](https://www.usenix.org/system/files/sec21-li-mengyuan.pdf) · [Website](https://cipherleaks.com/) · [BibTeX](https://mengyuanli.com/files/bib/cipherleaks-usenixsec21.bib)
- **[Exploiting Unprotected I/O Operations in AMD’s Secure Encrypted Virtualization](https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity19/presentation/li-mengyuan)**
  **Mengyuan Li**, Yinqian Zhang, Zhiqiang Lin, Yan Solihin
  *28th USENIX Security Symposium (USENIX Security 2019)*
  Studies attacks that exploit unprotected I/O operations in AMD SEV, highlighting early weaknesses in confidential VM designs.
  [Paper](https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity19/presentation/li-mengyuan) · [PDF](https://www.usenix.org/system/files/sec19-li-mengyuan_0.pdf) · [BibTeX](https://mengyuanli.com/files/bib/sev-io-usenixsec19.bib)

\* Equal contribution.

**Beyond TEEs:** Vulnerability research outside TEEs, such as [Chekhov’s Gun](https://mengyuanli.com/#chekhovs-gun-ccs25) on macOS sandboxing (ACM CCS 2025) and [VReaves](https://mengyuanli.com/#vreaves-arxiv25) on electromagnetic side channels (arXiv 2025), is in the [full publication list](https://mengyuanli.com/#publications).

## Defenses

- **[SoK: Understanding Design Choices and Pitfalls of Trusted Execution Environments](https://doi.org/10.1145/3634737.3644993)**
  **Mengyuan Li**, Yuheng Yang, Guoxing Chen, Mengjia Yan, Yinqian Zhang
  *19th ACM Asia Conference on Computer and Communications Security (ASIA CCS 2024)*
  A systems-oriented overview of TEE design tradeoffs and common pitfalls, useful for understanding how to build more secure confidential computing systems.
  [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1145/3634737.3644993) · [PDF](https://mengyuanli.com/files/asiaccs_sok.pdf) · [BibTeX](https://mengyuanli.com/files/bib/sok-tee-asiaccs24.bib)
- **[CipherH: Automated Detection of Ciphertext Side-channel Vulnerabilities in Cryptographic Implementations](https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity23/presentation/deng-sen)**
  Sen Deng, **Mengyuan Li**, Yining Tang, Shuai Wang, Shoumeng Yan, Yinqian Zhang
  *32nd USENIX Security Symposium (USENIX Security 2023)*
  Automatically detects program points in cryptographic software that are vulnerable to ciphertext side channels, finding over 200 in the RSA and ECDSA/ECDH implementations of OpenSSL, MbedTLS, and wolfSSL.
  [Paper](https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity23/presentation/deng-sen) · [PDF](https://www.usenix.org/system/files/usenixsecurity23-deng-sen.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/Sen-Deng/CipherH) · [BibTeX](https://mengyuanli.com/files/bib/cipherh-usenixsec23.bib)
- **[Defeating Speculative-Execution Attacks on SGX with HyperRace](https://doi.org/10.1109/DSC47296.2019.8937682)**
  Guoxing Chen, **Mengyuan Li**, Fengwei Zhang, Yinqian Zhang
  *2019 IEEE Conference on Dependable and Secure Computing (DSC 2019)*
  Addresses speculative-execution threats in SGX and reflects broader work on attack surfaces and mitigation around TEE platforms.
  [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1109/DSC47296.2019.8937682) · [PDF](https://yinqian.org/papers/idsc19.pdf) · [BibTeX](https://mengyuanli.com/files/bib/hyperrace-dsc19.bib)

# Verifiable AI

Mengyuan Li’s research on verifiable AI builds mechanisms that improve the integrity and auditability of deployed models. It focuses on verifying LLM inference and on how proof-based AI systems fail. The work connects verifiable AI with trustworthy machine learning systems and privacy-preserving oversight.

Topics: AI verification · zero-knowledge verification of LLM inference · trustworthy AI systems · model oversight

## Papers

- **[Hollow-LLM Attack: Computationally Trivial Weights in Zero-Knowledge Verification of LLM Inference](https://doi.org/10.1109/SP63933.2026.00258)**
  Chen Gong, Beijie Liu, **Mengyuan Li**
  *2026 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (S&P 2026)*
  Shows that a valid zero-knowledge proof of LLM inference is not proof of large-model execution: with “ghost weights”, a provider keeps the declared architecture and passes verification while paying only small-model cost.
  [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1109/SP63933.2026.00258) · [PDF](https://mengyuanli.com/files/hollow-llm.pdf) · [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28884) · [BibTeX](https://mengyuanli.com/files/hollow-llm.bib)
- **[WAVE: Leveraging Architecture Observation for Privacy-Preserving Model Oversight](https://doi.org/10.1145/3779212.3790247)**
  Haoxuan Xu\*, Chen Gong\*, Beijie Liu\*, Haizhong Zheng, Beidi Chen, **Mengyuan Li**
  *31st ACM International Conference on Architectural Support for Programming Languages and Operating Systems (ASPLOS 2026)*
  Explores privacy-preserving oversight of model execution: how to monitor and reason about model behavior in a trustworthy way.
  [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1145/3779212.3790247) · [Code](https://github.com/sept-usc/Wave) · [BibTeX](https://mengyuanli.com/files/bib/wave-asplos26.bib)

\* Equal contribution.

## Motivation

As AI systems become part of high-stakes workflows, users need evidence about which model produced a result and how it ran before they can trust it. That evidence should not reveal sensitive data. Verifiable AI sits at this boundary between systems, security, and machine learning.

## verifiable.pro

SEPT Lab maintains [verifiable.pro](https://verifiable.pro/), a public resource on verifiable AI. It publishes news, explainers, and guides on what evidence can establish about an AI service’s claims, starting from trusted execution environments. Its [verification stack](https://verifiable.pro/topics/) places each kind of claim in one of seven layers, from the chip up to the laws, standards, and agreements that govern an AI system.

## Related

**Other directions:** [AI Agent Security](https://mengyuanli.com/ai-agent-security.html) covers runtime monitoring and trusted infrastructure for LLM systems and agents; WAVE also belongs to that direction. [TEE and Confidential Computing](https://mengyuanli.com/tee-confidential-computing.html) covers the secure execution mechanisms that often support deployable verification pipelines.

**Lab:** The [SEPT Lab research overview](https://septlab.com/research.html) gives the broader lab context for this area.

---

Canonical page: https://mengyuanli.com/ai-agent-security.html

# AI Agent Security

Mengyuan Li’s research on AI agent security uses trusted execution environments (TEEs) and runtime monitoring to observe agent execution and to build trusted infrastructure for LLM systems and AI agents. The goal is agent backends that remain observable, trustworthy, and resilient when they run on shared cloud infrastructure and handle sensitive data.

Topics: secure AI agents · agent runtime monitoring · TEEs for AI agents · trusted infrastructure for LLM systems · trustworthy agent execution

## Perspective

This direction focuses on monitoring and protecting agent execution rather than only verifying final outputs. It brings together TEEs, confidential computing, and runtime observation to support trustworthy LLM systems and agentic infrastructure.

## Papers

- **[WAVE: Leveraging Architecture Observation for Privacy-Preserving Model Oversight](https://doi.org/10.1145/3779212.3790247)**
  Haoxuan Xu\*, Chen Gong\*, Beijie Liu\*, Haizhong Zheng, Beidi Chen, **Mengyuan Li**
  *31st ACM International Conference on Architectural Support for Programming Languages and Operating Systems (ASPLOS 2026)*
  Explores how system-level observation can support privacy-preserving monitoring of model execution, which aligns with runtime monitoring for trustworthy LLM systems and agents.
  [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1145/3779212.3790247) · [Code](https://github.com/sept-usc/Wave) · [BibTeX](https://mengyuanli.com/files/bib/wave-asplos26.bib)
- **[SCALE: Tackling Communication Bottlenecks in Confidential Distributed Machine Learning](https://doi.org/10.1109/HPCA68181.2026.11408582)**
  Joongun Park, Yongqin Wang, Huan Xu, Hanjiang Wu, **Mengyuan Li**, Tushar Krishna
  *2026 IEEE International Symposium on High-Performance Computer Architecture (HPCA 2026)*
  Contributes infrastructure for secure and efficient confidential multi-GPU execution, which is important for building trusted backends for large-scale LLM systems and agents.
  [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1109/HPCA68181.2026.11408582) · [BibTeX](https://mengyuanli.com/files/bib/scale-hpca26.bib)
- **[CatchBench: When Can an Agent Failure Be Caught?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22808)**
  Yue Zhao, **Mengyuan Li**, Ruolin Li, Prince Zizhuang Wang, Shuli Jiang, Linsey Pang, Xiongye Xiao, Xiyang Hu
  *arXiv preprint arXiv:2608.22808*
  Benchmarks when an agent failure can be caught by putting one auditor’s question to three information states: a run’s declared configuration, a growing prefix of its trace, and the finished trace.
  [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.22808) · [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22808) · [Code](https://github.com/yzhao062/catchbench) · [BibTeX](https://mengyuanli.com/files/bib/catchbench-arxiv26.bib)
- **[Behavioral Skill Reconstruction: Reconstructing Hidden Functionality from LLM Agent Skills](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04192)**
  Peichun Hua, Haoxuan Xu, **Mengyuan Li**
  *arXiv preprint arXiv:2608.04192*
  Shows that keeping an LLM agent skill’s files secret does not keep its functionality secret: through ordinary use alone, the black-box attack SkillClone recovers several of 30 tested skills exactly or partially.
  [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.04192) · [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04192) · [BibTeX](https://mengyuanli.com/files/bib/skill-reconstruction-arxiv26.bib)
- **[Infrastructure for Valuable, Tradable, and Verifiable Agent Memory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.24564)**
  **Mengyuan Li**, Lei Gao, Haoxuan Xu, Jiate Li, Potung Yu, Lingke Cheng, Yue Zhao, Murali Annavaram
  *arXiv preprint arXiv:2603.24564*
  Proposes infrastructure that makes agent memory verifiable and tradable: ClawGang binds memory to verifiable computational provenance through TEE remote attestation, and MeowTrade is a market layer for listing, transferring, and governing certified memory artifacts.
  [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.24564) · [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.24564) · [Code](https://github.com/sept-usc/ClawGang) · [BibTeX](https://mengyuanli.com/files/bib/agent-memory-arxiv26.bib)

\* Equal contribution.

## Projects

**Open source:**

- **[ClawGang](https://clawgang.ai/)**
  Infrastructure for valuable, tradable, and verifiable agent memory. ClawGang binds agent memory to verifiable computational provenance through TEE-based certification on AMD SEV-SNP.
  [Website](https://clawgang.ai/) · [Code](https://github.com/sept-usc/ClawGang)
- **[Muse MCP Adapter](https://github.com/sept-usc/muse-mcp-adapter)**
  A user-controlled bridge between the Muse personal agent and MCP servers. The agent sees only the capabilities the user has reviewed, and every write is confirmed by the user first and runs at most once.
  [Code](https://github.com/sept-usc/muse-mcp-adapter)
- **[WAVE artifact](https://github.com/sept-usc/Wave)**
  Artifact for the ASPLOS 2026 paper [WAVE: Leveraging Architecture Observation for Privacy-Preserving Model Oversight](https://mengyuanli.com/ai-agent-security.html#wave-asplos26).
  [Code](https://github.com/sept-usc/Wave)

## Foundations

[TEE and Confidential Computing](https://mengyuanli.com/tee-confidential-computing.html) provide mechanisms for isolated execution, protection of agent state, and secure multi-tenant infrastructure.

[Verifiable AI](https://mengyuanli.com/verifiable-ai.html) is related because agent systems also need execution integrity, auditability, and trustworthy model-serving pipelines.

## Challenges

Key open problems include:

- observing agent execution with TEEs or runtime monitoring;
- isolating tool execution;
- protecting long-lived memory and secrets;
- building trusted infrastructure for LLM systems and agents;
- defending agent backends against cloud- and hardware-level leakage.

## Related

**Teaching:** [CSCI 699: Understanding and Identifying Side-Channel Threats in Cloud and LLM Systems](https://mengyuanli.com/25fall_699.html) covers threat models that matter when agents and LLM systems run on shared infrastructure.

**Lab:** [SEPT Lab](https://septlab.com/) studies systems and security problems that connect to the foundations of AI agent security, especially where secure execution and trustworthy infrastructure meet AI workloads.

Canonical page: https://mengyuanli.com/25fall_699.html

# CSCI 699: Understanding and Identifying Side-Channel Threats in Cloud and LLM Systems

Graduate seminar on side-channel attacks across multi-tenant cloud platforms, TEEs, GPUs, and LLM services.

Fall 2025 · Thursday 3:30-6:50pm · DMC 211

## Overview

- **Units:** 4.0
- **Term—Day—Time:** Fall 2025, Thursday 3:30-6:50pm
- **Location:** DMC 211
- **Instructor:** Mengyuan Li
- **Office:** GCS 502A
- **Office Hours:** Wednesday 11am-12 pm, GCS, B2 floor-SB9
- **Contact Info:** [mli49061@usc.edu](mailto:mli49061@usc.edu) (Please include “CSCI 699” in your email subject.)
- **Teaching Assistant:** TBD
- **Slides & Materials:** Shared via the Google Drive folder

## Description

This graduate seminar course provides an in-depth exploration of side-channel attacks with a focus on cloud computing environments and large language model (LLM) systems. We will examine how subtle indirect leakages (e.g., execution timing, cache usage, resource contention) can breach isolation barriers in multi-tenant clouds and reveal sensitive data from cryptographic operations, cloud VMs/containers, and even modern AI models. Students will study both foundational side-channel techniques (cache timing attacks, speculative execution vulnerabilities) and cutting-edge research on side channels targeting cloud infrastructure and LLM deployments.

## Objectives

- Taxonomy & Fundamentals: Understand the taxonomy of side-channel attacks (timing, cache, power, etc.) and why they pose threats to secure cloud computing. Grasp fundamental techniques like cache Flush+Reload and Prime+Probe, branch prediction manipulation, and other microarchitectural exploits.
- Cloud Multi-Tenancy Risks: Analyze how cloud features (VM co-residency, shared hardware like last-level caches, GPUs) enable cross-tenant side-channel leaks.
- Speculative Execution Vulnerabilities: Comprehend transient execution attacks (e.g., Meltdown, Spectre) that exploit out-of-order and speculative execution to leak protected memory.
- A better understanding of other common privacy-preserving computation techniques such as FL, MPC, and FHE.
- Improve academic writing and presentation skills through assignments and the final project.

## Grading

- Assessment Tool | % of Grade
- Assignment 1 | 15%
- Assignment 2 | 15%
- Course Presentation | 20%
- Final Project | 40%
- Participation and Discussion | 10%

## Schedule

- Week | Date | Topics/Daily Activities | Readings/Preparation | Deliverables
- 1 | Aug 28 | Introduction to Side Channel | Course syllabus, Introductory articles on cloud security | -
- 2 | Sept 04 | Microarchitecture Side-channels | Relevant research papers about cache side channel | -
- 3 | Sept 11 | Side Channels in Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) | Articles on CVMs and cloud implementations | -
- 4 | Sept 18 | Programming with fingerprinting webpages | Tutorial on VMs and QEMU (related website: [QEMU and KVM](https://bitgrounds.tech/posts/kvm-qemu-libvirt-virtualization/)) | Assignment 1.1 Assigned
- 5 | Sept 25 | Transient Execution Attacks; Assignment 1.2 Demo | 2-3 relevant research papers | Assignment 1.1 Check-in/ Assignment 1.2 Assigned
- 6 | Oct 2 | Beyond microarchitecture side channel – Frequency, Port Contention, and Other Channels | 2-3 relevant research papers | -
- 7 | Oct 9 | Side-Channel Attacks on GPUs | 2-3 relevant research papers | Assignment 1 Due/Assignment 2.1 Assigned
- 8 | Oct 16 | Side-Channel Inference of ML Models (DNNs) | 2-3 relevant research papers about GPU vulnerabilities | Assignment 2.1 Due/Assignment 2.2 Assigned

- 10 | Oct 30 | Programming with ML side-channel attacks | - | -

- 16 | Dec 11 | Final Project Report Due | - | Project Final Report Due

# CSCI 699: Confidential Computing: Protecting Your Data on Cloud GPUs and CPUs

Graduate course on trusted execution environments, confidential VMs, and confidential GPUs, together with related privacy techniques such as federated learning, secure multi-party computation, and fully homomorphic encryption.

Spring 2025 · Thursday 4:00-7:20pm · Social Sciences Building

## Overview

- **Units:** 4.0
- **Term—Day—Time:** Spring 2025, Thursday 4:00-7:20pm
- **Location:** Social Sciences Building
- **Instructor:** Mengyuan Li
- **Office:** GCS 502A
- **Office Hours:** Wednesday 11am-12 pm, GCS, B2 floor-SB4
- **Contact Info:** [mli49061@usc.edu](mailto:mli49061@usc.edu) (Please include “CSCI 699” in your email subject.)
- **Teaching Assistant:** TBD
- **Slides & Materials:** Shared via the Google Drive folder

## Description

This course offers an in-depth study of confidential computing and privacy-preserving computational techniques, focusing on protecting data in cloud environments using both CPUs and GPUs. Students will explore the design and implementation of Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) and examine various cloud services that support confidential computing, including secure enclaves, Confidential Virtual Machines (CVMs), and confidential GPUs.

## Objectives

- A comprehensive understanding of confidential computing and TEE.
- Gain experience in reading, analyzing, and critically evaluating research papers.
- Understand and experiment with state-of-the-art systems related to TEEs and CVMs.
- A better understanding of other common privacy-preserving computation techniques such as FL, MPC, and FHE.
- Improve academic writing and presentation skills through assignments and the final project.

## Grading

- Assessment Tool | % of Grade
- Assignment 1 | 15%
- Assignment 2 | 15%
- Course Presentation | 20%
- Final Project | 40%
- Participation and Discussion | 10%
